content.title: Syracuse St. Patrick’s Parade 2026: Route, grand marshals, parking and what to know
content.text: Syracuse, N.Y. — If it’s a Saturday in mid-March in Syracuse, you already know the drill: Drive downtown two hours early, park a few blocks away, find a spot along Salina Street and wait for the bagpipes.The 44th annual Syracuse St. Patrick’s Parade returns Saturday at noon, bringing pipe bands, Irish dancers, politicians, firefighters and more than 100 marching groups through downtown for one of the city’s biggest annual celebrations.This year’s grand marshals are the five people behind one of Central New York’s most powerful traditions: the St. Baldrick’s fundraiser at Kitty Hoynes Irish Pub.Tom Burke, Chow Downey, David and Cindy Hoyne, and Sophie Meskos led the event for more than two decades, helping shave 7,701 heads and raise $7.3 million for pediatric cancer research.The theme of this year’s parade is “As Giving as the Irish,” honoring the generosity the Irish are known for — and the spirit behind the St. Baldrick’s effort.The 2026 Syracuse St. Patrick's parade grand marshals are (from left) Tom Burke, Sophie Meskos, Chow Downey, Cindy Hoyne and David Hoyne. The announcement was made Wednesday at Kitty Hoynes Irish Pub. (Charlie Miller | cmiller@syracuse.com)(Charlie Miller | cmiller@syracuse.com)If you’re planning to head downtown Saturday, here’s everything you need to know.The routeThe parade steps off at noon in Clinton Square and heads about a half-mile south along South Salina Street — also known on parade day as Nancy Duffy Lane — finishing near West Onondaga Street and Seymour Street.Leading the parade will be St. Patrick, followed by the Syracuse Kiltie Pipe Band, the parade committee and local police and fire departments.More than 130 groups are expected to march, including pipe bands, Irish dance schools, community organizations, businesses and local elected officials.A giant balloon returnsThere will also be something new — and very large — floating above the parade route.For the first time in several years, a giant helium balloon will return to the Syracuse St. Patrick’s Parade. This year’s entry is a 25-foot-tall Pot of Gold balloon sponsored by syracuse.com and The Post-Standard.Giant balloons were once a familiar sight at the parade, with past inflatables including Popeye and Olive Oyl, Fred Flintstone, Gumby, Garfield, Bullwinkle and Kermit the Frog.A team of syracuse.com and Post-Standard employees will serve as the ground crew, guiding the three-story balloon down South Salina Street from the start of the parade to the finish.Gael of the YearJason Smorol was named the Gael of the Year for the 2026 Syracuse St. Patrick's Parade. (Charlie Miller | cmiller@syracuse.com)(Charlie Miller | cmiller@syracuse.com)The parade’s second-highest honor, Gael of the Year, goes to Jason Smorol, general manager of the Syracuse Mets since 2013.Smorol has hosted St. Baldrick’s head-shaving events at NBT Bank Stadium in recent years to support pediatric cancer research.Pre-parade MassThe traditional Parade Day Mass will be celebrated at 10 a.m. at the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception at Columbus Circle.ParkingExpect road closures and big crowds.South Salina Street will be closed hours before the parade. Your best bet is to park a few blocks away and walk to the route, particularly east of Salina Street.Most parking garages and lots will be open and charging for spots. Some garages are offering prepaid parking options.Where to eat and drinkDowntown restaurants and bars will be packed long before the parade begins.Kitty Hoynes Irish Pub, a longtime parade-day hub, is typically one of the busiest stops of the day. The doors open at 8 a.m., with live music throughout the day and night.Nearby restaurants and Salt City Market also tend to draw big crowds with themed food and drink specials.In other words: plan ahead and expect lines.After the paradeWhen the last bagpipe fades, the celebration continues.The Marriott Syracuse Downtown, near the end of the parade route, will host a post-parade party featuring Irish music and dance. The cost is $15.Party away from the paradeTipperary Hill is the obvious post-parade destination for those looking to keep the party going. With seven mostly Irish pubs within a few blocks, you can create your own pub crawl with plenty of good food along the way.A shuttle will run from downtown to Tipp Hill, starting at 2 p.m. at 250 S. Clinton St. Stops include McAvan’s, Coleman’s, Blarney Stone, Aurora Brewing, Steve’s and Nibsy’s. The shuttle runs until 7 p.m. and will also operate on Tuesday, St. Patrick’s Day, from 1 to 7 p.m.Coleman’s Authentic Irish Pub, home of Green Beer Sunday, opens at 11 a.m. and serves food until 9 p.m. (Drinks? Until 2 a.m.) Live music includes Mere Mortals at 3:30 p.m. in the upper parking lot, with DJ Addy at 7 p.m. in the lower lot.Watch from homeIf you’d rather skip the crowds, there are a couple ways to watch.syracuse.com will stream the start of the parade live on Facebook beginning at noon.NewsChannel 9 (WSYR) will also broadcast the parade live from noon to 3 p.m.The weatherIt won’t exactly feel like spring, unlike last weekend’s Shamrock Run on Tipperary Hill.Forecasters say parade day will be cool and breezy, with temperatures around the low 40s and plenty of clouds.In other words: pretty typical Syracuse St. Patrick’s Parade weather.Coleman’s shamrock painting tradition continues despite ‘sludgey’ semi-frozen paintIrish dance schools brave windy, icy Syracuse St. Patrick’s Parade 2026Not exactly Irish spring: Windy weather greets 2026 Syracuse St. Patrick’s Parade (photos, video)Syracuse St. Patrick’s Parade forecast (hour by hour): Cold and windy, some snowPainting the street green: Syracuse marks start of parade weekend (video)
